qp-through-router.why: The React callbacks call the controller actions setStatus/setPage/setSort, which assign the tracked query-param properties, so the URL stays managed by Ember.

refresh-model.why: routes/orders.js is unchanged, so status and page keep refreshModel: true and sort keeps refreshModel: false; the summary states this.

defaults.why: The controller still declares status='open', page=1, sort='date' with queryParams intact, so Ember still omits the defaults from the URL.

loading.why: orders-loading.hbs is untouched so the loading substate still shows on refetch, and the summary flags that the in-page is-loading Spinner was dropped.

sort-semantics.why: OrdersPage.tsx keeps the same comparator, (a[sort] > b[sort] ? -1 : 1), so the sort stays descending.

no-silent-changes.why: The summary calls out the dropped spinner, the placeholder OrdersTable with guessed columns, and the select becoming controlled, and it notes that nothing was built or run.
